messages:
Matt: Ran a latency vs throughput sweep this morning across us-west -> us-east routing with a few knobs: microbatch sizes [1,4,8], kernel variant A (fused-attn optimized) vs B (fallback cuBLAS path), and KV cache cold/hot toggles. Results are weird — p95 ok, p99 jumps when fallback kicks in.
Anya: Can you paste the experiment matrix and the numbers? also which model + seq len?
Matt: Model: open-v2-medium, seq 512 typical, burst profile from UI tests. Quick table: microbatch=1 p95~120ms p99~420ms; microbatch=4 p95~140ms p99~700ms; microbatch=8 p95~190ms p99~1.1s. BUT when routing cross-region fallback happens (requests routed us-west -> us-east for cold spare) p99 sometimes hits 2.4s.
Sara: That 2.4s looks like network+cache miss. Did you capture KV cache hit rate on the fallback path?
Matt: Yes — hot path KV hit ~92%. Fallback path (us-east) had KV cold for ~12% of requests during the test (we were spinning new shards). So two factors: kernel queuing + remote cache miss. Perf traces attached: https://perf.internal/fg/1769901234
Devin: Any kernel-level differences between A and B for the tail? e.g. A has lower median but bigger variance?
Matt: Exactly. Variant A (our fused kernels) gives lower median and p95, but when multiple microbatches line up it can create an intra-GPU queueing effect that amplifies tail. Variant B is slightly slower median but smoother tail because it spreads smaller kernel launches. I saw kernel latencies with A: median 0.9ms, tail 12ms; B: median 1.3ms, tail 5ms.
Kevin: Did you check memcpy staging and host->device queue bursts? we've seen memcpy spikes cause p99 before.
Matt: Yup — transcript from perf agent shows memcpy bursts correlating with fallback RPCs. When fallback to us-east happens we get an extra 60-80ms of transfer and lock contention on the KV client, which blocks request handling until KV returns. Combined with a queued kernel burst, that makes the p99 explode.
Anya: Can you share the quick repro config? want to try a controlled run with pinned KV shards + artificially injected network latency.
Matt: Config snippet used:
```
routing:
  primary: us-west
  fallback: us-east
  fallback_policy: region_capacity
microbatch:
  sizes: [1,4,8]
kernel_variant: [A,B]
kv_cache:
  mode: auto
  prewarm: false
```
Sara: For SLO tuning we should measure p95 vs p99 tradeoff in two dimensions: (1) microbatch size sweep with kernel A/B; (2) routing policy: prefer-local vs capacity-first. If prefer-local avoids cross-region fallbacks we might keep microbatch=4 and kernel A but prewarm KV.
Devin: Also try aggressive prewarm on fallback region (simple warm-up on rollout) and set the KV client to optimistic async fetch (so we serve partial responses while fetching). Could reduce the blocking window.
Kevin: Two quick immediate mitigations I'd try: 1) tighten fallback threshold so we avoid brief cross-region spins; 2) set microbatch cap to 4 for routes with cross-region potential. Both are low risk.
Matt: Agree. I scheduled a controlled run at 12:30 PT with these changes. Will upload flame graphs + perf agent logs. perf-bot: run-id 2026-03-17-12-30 created.
perf-bot: Job started: perf-sweep/1769901234-run1 — collecting GPU traces, KV metrics, and RPC latencies.
Anya: Nice. After the run, let's graph p99 vs throughput line for each kernel variant and produce a short recommendation for Console (auto-suggestion) around microbatch settings.
Matt: Will do. Early takeaway: kernel selection matters for median, but routing+KV behavior dominates p99 when cross-region fallback occurs. We should treat routing flakiness as a first-class input to SLO tuning.
Sara: +1. Also add a gating rule: if KV prewarm < 80% for fallback region, avoid routing there for SLO-sensitive routes. :white_check_mark:
Matt: Good call. I'll post results and a short RFC with config patches later today.
Devin: Thanks — ping us when the logs are up.
Matt: Will do.
